title: Cultivation of cannabis vs possession - separate offences explained
p1:
Having cannabis and growing cannabis may sound like the same legal issue. But the law can treat them as two very different offences.

And that distinction can significantly affect the consequences a person faces.
p2:
A common misconception is that growing a cannabis plant is simply another form of possessing cannabis.

In reality, possession generally concerns having control over cannabis, while cultivation concerns the act of growing or producing the plant.

Here is the surprising part: A person may face a cultivation allegation even when there is a separate question about whether they personally possessed or controlled the harvested cannabis.
p3:
Consider two situations.

Someone found carrying cannabis may face a possession charge. Someone growing cannabis plants may face a cultivation charge, even if no harvested cannabis is found.

The evidence can also differ. Possession cases may focus on control, knowledge and the substance itself. Cultivation cases may focus on plants, growing activity and the person's involvement.

One incident can potentially involve both offences, depending on the applicable law and evidence.

The practical takeaway? Never assume that proving possession automatically proves cultivation, or that disproving possession necessarily defeats a cultivation allegation. Each offence has its own legal elements.
conclusion: Should cultivation and possession be treated as separate offences with distinct legal requirements, even when they arise from the same incident? What is your view?
